course_description:
This course introduces students to the mathematical and computational aspects of statistical modeling. Emphasis is placed on a precise understanding of randomness and probability distributions, and statistical methods such as estimation, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, regression and linear models and categorical data analysis . The course also covers exploratory data analysis, the design of experiments and ethical research, as well as the importance of critical thinking and communication in the interpretation of results.

STAT1301 is an advanced version of STAT1201, meant for first-year students who would like to more fully understand the mathematical reasoning, critical thinking and computational techniques involved in probability and statistics. Each week students will attend lectures, as well as an applied class (starting in week 2). Emphasis will be placed on fundamental topics such as sampling, probability and statistical models, probability distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, regression, linear models, and statistical computation. The tutorial and assignment questions are designed to apply and test these concepts, provide students with feedback and help with preparation towards the exam.

course_aims: The aim of STAT1301 is to provide an understanding of the nature of scientific data, the subsequent need for statistical analysis, and an introduction to the mathematics underpinning these methods. You will develop your statistical expertise and critical judgement in scientific studies, including an awareness of ethical issues in research and analysis. You will learn how probability models and simple mathematical ideas provide the foundation for statistical inference. You will use these models to draw conclusions from data, assess assumptions, and explore data visually using statistical software.

learning_outcomes.description: Explain the nature of scientific data and the need for statistical analysis.
Construct probabilistic models of random phenomena and derive quantities of interest including expectation and variance.
Explain the behaviour of hypothesis tests under null and alternative hypotheses, including Type I error rates, power, and the interpretation of p-values.
Identify and critically evaluate ethical issues in scientific research.
Demonstrate a foundational knowledge of statistical methods by being able to carry out simple statistical procedures by hand.
Use statistical software appropriately and confidently for exploratory data analysis and to make relevant statistical conclusions.
Plan and carry out a research project, and analyse and communicate the results.

assessment_details.task_description: You must attend your applied classes in person. In each class, you will receive a task sheet containing activities designed to support your learning, including questions modelled on the style of STAT1301 exam questions. Some tasks may also require you to write R code. Each applied class exercise will be marked out of 1. You may work in groups on the provided task. To earn the point, you must arrive on time, remain engaged with the task throughout the session, and contribute to the written solutions. Your mark for this component will be calculated from your best eight of ten applied class exercises. This means you may miss two applied classes without penalty. Applied class scores will be uploaded to Blackboard the week after the class runs. It is your responsibility to check these marks and follow the procedure outlined on Blackboard if you have any concerns or think that a mark has been missed. Deferral or extension
You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
If you are unable to attend your scheduled class, you should attend another applied class in the same week where possible.
You may miss two applied class exercises without penalty because your mark for this component will be calculated from your best eight of ten exercises.
If you are unable to attend more than two applied classes’ assessments, please email STAT1301@uq.edu.au to explain your circumstances, including an explanation of why you are/were unable to attend another session in the same week. You will need to do this within 5 calendar days of your applied class, and include appropriate evidence (e.g., medical certificate) covering the week for which you are seeking an exemption. If approved, you will be given an exemption from that assessment, and your remaining marks will be reweighted. For example, with one exemption your mark will be taken from your best 7 out of 9 marks. You can receive at most two exemptions during the semester.
